title: Nectar robbing by bees affects the reproductive fitness of the distylous plant Tirpitzia sinensis (Linaceae)
rationale: Geometry is compared between robbed and unrobbed flowers within morphs; legitimate visitation rate is not the geometry response.

title: Plant–animal interactions in suburban environments: implications for floral evolution
rationale: Focal geometry result is corolla traits versus proportion of flowers robbed; mutualist outcomes exist in the broader study but are not a matched route-rate decomposition for the geometry effect.

title: Preferential nectar robbing of flowers with long corollas: experimental studies of two hummingbird species visiting three plant species
rationale: Fixed artificial-flower arrays and focal natural flowers were offered under defined observation periods; legitimate and robbing visits were counted separately and unvisited flowers remained in the opportunity set.

title: Pollinators and nectar robbers cause directional selection for large spur circle in Impatiens oxyanthera (Balsaminaceae)
rationale: Pollinator and nectar-robber visit frequencies were measured as No. h-1 on the same focal plants, including zero frequencies, and modeled separately against floral traits.

title: Nectar robbing as a mechanism of biotic resistance against an invasive plant in the Galápagos Islands
rationale: Focal geometry models predict robbery probability/intensity from corolla dimensions; legitimate visitation is rare and not estimated as the paired geometry response.

title: Long corollas as nectar barriers in Lonicera implexa: interactions between corolla tube length and nectar volume
rationale: Focal response is flower robbery frequency as a function of corolla length and reward traits.

title: Floral traits variation, legitimate pollination, and nectar robbing in Polygala vayredae (Polygalaceae)
rationale: The same flowers have robbery intensity and successful-versus-unsuccessful pollination status, but legitimate interaction is a pollination-success state rather than an absolute legitimate visitation rate; strict both-route rate identifiability is therefore not met.

title: Integrating morphological and molecular perspectives on foraging tactic constancy in a nectar-robbing bumble bee
rationale: Morphology is related to tactic class (legitimate, robber, switcher) among foragers; no explicit no-interaction opportunity denominator is identified.

title: Geographic distribution and trait-mediated causes of nectar robbing by the European bumblebee Bombus terrestris on the Patagonian shrub Fuchsia magellanica
rationale: Focal response is incidence/probability of primary nectar robbing versus petal length and robber glossa length.

title: Illegitimate flower visitors and pollinators are associated with different flower morphology: Evidence from five species of Penstemon (Plantaginaceae)
rationale: Focal response is nectar-robbing occurrence across Penstemon morphology.

title: Floral trait variation across individual plants within a population enhances defense capability to nectar robbing
rationale: Common plant observation periods recorded visitor-type frequencies as visits per flower per hour; legitimate and robber visitation were separately available with zero frequencies possible.

title: Hyper-specialization for long-billed bird pollination in a guild of South African plants: the Malachite Sunbird pollination syndrome
rationale: Legitimate versus robbery use was route-resolved across observed bird-plant interactions, but the archived audit does not establish a common no-interaction opportunity denominator for both routes.

title: Nectar robbing, forager efficiency and seed set: Bumblebees foraging on the self incompatible plant Linaria vulgaris (Scrophulariaceae)
rationale: Bumblebee tongue-length classes are related to legitimate versus robbing tactic use among flower users; interaction absence is not the focal denominator.

title: Nectar robbing does not affect female reproductive success of an endangered Antirrhinum species, Plantaginaceae
rationale: Focal response is nectar-robbing occurrence / percentage of robbed flowers among populations.

title: The conspicuously large bracts influence reproductive success in Thunia alba (Orchidaceae)
rationale: Bract-removal experiment used common observation effort and recorded normal versus robbery visits separately (16/3 intact; 5/21 removed), with treatment-level visit frequency also reported.

title: Is bee‐avoidance by bird‐pollinated flowers driven by nectar robbing in Erica ?
rationale: Focal population response is nectar-robbing rate versus corolla length and other floral covariates; bypass/legitimate absolute route rates are not separately identified.

title: Bird extinctions shift bill–flower trait matching in Hawaiian lobelioids
rationale: Published analysis models nectar-robbing probability as bill-flower matching changes among recorded interactions.

title: Soil moisture influences nectar robbing and plant fitness in a primrose species
rationale: Focal geometry pathway is flower accessibility versus plot-level nectar-robbing intensity; switching behavior is documented but a paired legitimate route-rate geometry model is not identified in the audited evidence.

title: Long corolla flowers in Tropical Andes favour nectar robbing by the Black Metaltail hummingbird: A study using citizen science and field observations
rationale: Citizen-science and field foraging events are classified as legitimate versus robbery; robbery percentage is conditional on observed foraging events.

title: When Bigger Is not Better: Corolla Length Increases Nectar Robbing in Aloe secundiflora Engl. (Asphodelaceae)
rationale: Focal result is greater probability of nectar robbing with longer corollas.

title: Effects of nectar robbing on nectar dynamics and bumblebee foraging strategies in Linaria vulgaris (Scrophulariaceae)
rationale: On nine sunny days, standardized five-minute patch observations were repeated across sites; every visiting bumblebee was identified and classified as legitimate or robbing. Figure 2 reports absolute mean numbers of legitimate and primary/secondary robbing bees under the same observation windows, so zero counts are retained in a common time denominator.

title: Relationship between floral tube length and nectar robbing in Duranta erecta L. (Verbenaceae)
rationale: Focal response is probability that a flower was robbed versus flower length and diameter.

title: Effect of Weigela hortensis (Caprifoliaceae) floral morphology on pollinator behavior
rationale: Foraging behavior and robbery frequency are contrasted between sites/accessibility states among flower visits; no explicit zero-interaction opportunity denominator is reported in the audited evidence.

title: Nectar robbing: a common phenomenon mainly determined by accessibility constraints, nectar volume and density of energy rewards
rationale: Focal multi-community response is proportion of flowers robbed versus flower length and protective/access traits.

title: The flowerpiercers interactions with a community of high Andean plants
rationale: Focal species-level response is nectar-robbing frequency versus effective corolla length and rewards.

title: Floral visitors of sesame (Sesamum indicum L.): Elucidating their nectar-robbing behaviour and impacts on the plant reproduction
rationale: Each corolla treatment reports total visitor abundance as visitors per flower per 10 min and the percentage of visits that were robbing under the same sampling design; route-specific absolute rates are therefore derivable from the common effort denominator.

title: Nectar robbery in Campsidium valdivianum: observations on floral morphology and the role of bumblebees and birds in southern Chile
rationale: Focal response is small/large robbery perforation occurrence versus corolla dimensions.

title: Catching the thief: Nectar robbing behaviour by bumblebees on naturalised Fuchsia magellanica in Ireland
rationale: Flower-level outcome is whether a flower was robbed versus flower size.

title: Geographic variation in resistance to nectar robbing and consequences for pollination
rationale: Pollinator visits and Xylocopa robber visits were each analyzed as visits per hour for the same plants, using only observation days when the plant had open flowers; zero visits are retained through log(x+1).

title: Correlations among traits associated with herbivore resistance and pollination: implications for pollination and nectar robbing in a distylous plant
rationale: Focal morphology tests use plant-level nectar-robbing level as outcome; legitimate route rate is not the paired response.

title: Nectar robbing from Hibiscus flowers by White-eyes on an oceanic island, Chichi-jima, Bonin Islands
rationale: Primary report relates larger flower size to higher robbery frequency; no separately estimable legitimate route rate is identified.

title: Geographic Variation in Flower Size and Flower-Visitor Composition of Two Bumblebee-Pollinated, Spring-Flowering Herbs, Lamium album L. var. barbatum (Lamiaceae) and Meehania urticifolia (Lamiaceae)
rationale: Focal geometry evidence uses bite-mark/robbery occurrence and population robbery severity versus calyx dimensions; legitimate route rate is not the paired geometry response.

title: Morphological constraints and nectar robbing in three Andean bumble bee species (Hymenoptera, Apidae, Bombini)
rationale: Bumblebee species with different reach are classified by legitimate versus robbing route on Digitalis; audited evidence does not supply a common zero-inclusive opportunity denominator.
